Apple Music's upcoming feature will let you record yourself doing karaoke

By Kamali

Apple Music is adding a karaoke video feature called Selfie Sing, which lets iPhone users film themselves with the front camera while singing along to on-screen lyrics, then save or share the clip. The feature was spotted in the first iOS 27.3 developer beta, with a public release expected in December.

Apple Music is preparing a new karaoke-style feature called Selfie Sing that lets people record videos of themselves singing without leaving the app. The feature appeared in the first developer beta of iOS 27.3, which Apple released on November 3, 2026, and a public release is expected in December.

What Selfie Sing does

With Selfie Sing, an iPhone user can sing along to a song while the front-facing camera records them, with the lyrics shown on screen. According to the description shown in the feature, users can adjust the vocal effects on their voice, then save the video or share the performance with friends. Until now, anyone who wanted to make a singing video would typically have to switch to another app to film it.

The feature builds on Apple Music Sing, the karaoke mode that Apple introduced in late 2022 with iOS 16.2. That tool lets listeners reduce the original singer's vocals and follow animated lyrics. Selfie Sing adds the camera on top of it.

Who found it and how to try it

The feature was first spotted by Aaron Perris in iOS 27.3 beta 1. Beta users can find it by searching Apple Music for a playlist named Selfie Sing. Tech sites report that the playlist is visible even on iPhones running iOS 27.2, but the option to turn on the camera and record only appears on the iOS 27.3 beta.

Early limits

The feature is clearly still in testing. Coverage of early hands-on use says only a small number of songs support it so far, with one report counting six. It also appears to be limited to iPhones. AppleInsider reported that the camera option did not show up on an iPad Pro running the iPadOS 27.3 beta. Aaron Perris's demonstration video used an Animoji in place of his face, but reports say Selfie Sing does not support Animoji yet.

Other changes in the beta

Selfie Sing is not the only Apple Music change in this beta. 9to5Mac reports that iOS 27.3 also improves the lyrics view when the phone is held in landscape orientation.

What is still unknown

Beta features can change or be removed before release, so the final version of Selfie Sing may look different. It is not yet clear how many songs will be supported at launch, whether it will come to the iPad or other devices, what the sharing options will be, or whether it will be available in every region where Apple Music operates. Apple has not published detailed information about the feature in the coverage reviewed.

Why it matters

Short singing videos are a popular form of content on social platforms, and music services have been looking for ways to give listeners more to do than press play. By adding recording and sharing directly to Apple Music, Apple is making its app a place where people can create content as well as listen. If Selfie Sing launches broadly in December, it could also give Apple Music subscribers a reason to spend more time in the app and put it in competition with the karaoke and video features of other music and social apps.
